# Content Recommendation Method, Device, and System

## Overview

The present disclosure presents a content recommendation method, device, and system designed to deliver personalized content to users through an adaptive, feedback-driven approach. The system initially recommends content from a predefined content set based on an average recommendation probability, providing a balanced starting point before user-specific preferences are established.

## Feedback Collection Mechanism

A central feature of the system is its ability to collect feedback information from the user's client. This feedback comprises two distinct types of data: display information and click information. Together, these data types provide a comprehensive picture of how users interact with the recommended content.

The **display information** captures the details of content presentation, including both the number of times specific content has been displayed and the precise timing of these displays. In parallel, the **click information** records user engagement by tracking the number of clicks on the client as well as the timing associated with each click action. By capturing both the frequency and temporal patterns of these interactions, the system gains nuanced insight into user behavior.

## Determining Preferred Content

Based on the collected feedback information, the system determines a sequence of preferred contents from the content set. This ordered sequence serves to guide subsequent recommendations, ensuring that the content presented to the user becomes increasingly aligned with their demonstrated interests over time. As feedback accumulates, the recommendation process continuously refines its output to better reflect individual preferences.

## Advantages

A significant advantage of this feedback-based approach is its effectiveness even in challenging scenarios. Specifically, the system is capable of delivering reasonable and effective content recommendations for random users who exhibit relatively few click behaviors. By leveraging both display and click information—rather than relying solely on explicit click actions—the method overcomes the limitations of sparse user engagement, thereby extending high-quality recommendations to a broader range of users.

# Content Recommendation Method Based on Average Recommendation Probability and User Feedback

## Technical Field

This disclosure relates to the field of information technology, and more particularly to a content recommendation method that improves recommendation performance by leveraging comprehensive user feedback, including display and click information.

## Background

Content recommendation systems have become integral to modern digital platforms, helping users discover relevant information from vast amounts of available content. Traditional recommendation approaches often rely heavily on user click behavior as the primary signal for determining user preferences. While this approach works reasonably well for highly engaged users who frequently interact with recommended content, it presents significant limitations when applied to certain user segments.

In particular, so-called "random users"—those who exhibit fewer click actions or engage sparingly with recommended content—pose a considerable challenge. Because these users generate limited click data, conventional systems struggle to accurately infer their preferences, resulting in poor recommendation quality and diminished user experience. This shortcoming reduces the overall effectiveness of recommendation systems in low-engagement scenarios.

## Summary of the Disclosure

To address these limitations, this disclosure presents a content recommendation method that combines average recommendation probability with comprehensive user feedback to determine a sequence of preferred contents for subsequent recommendations.

The method operates in two principal phases. In the first phase, content is recommended to a user based on an average recommendation probability. This average recommendation probability provides a baseline metric for selecting and presenting candidate content, ensuring that users receive relevant recommendations even in the absence of extensive historical interaction data.

In the second phase, the system collects user feedback in response to the recommended content. Notably, this feedback encompasses more than simple click behavior. It includes both display information and click information, capturing rich contextual details such as the number of times content is displayed, the timing of those displays, the number of clicks, and the timing of those clicks. By analyzing these multiple dimensions of user interaction, the system develops a more nuanced understanding of user preferences.

Based on this collected feedback, the method determines a sequence of preferred contents. This preference sequence is then used to inform and refine subsequent content recommendations, creating a continuous feedback loop that progressively improves recommendation accuracy over time.

## Advantages

A key advantage of this approach lies in its ability to leverage comprehensive user feedback rather than relying solely on click behavior. By incorporating display information—such as how often and when content is shown to a user—alongside click information, the method can extract meaningful preference signals even from users who click infrequently.

As a result, the disclosed method enables reasonable and effective content recommendation for random users and other low-engagement audiences who exhibit fewer click actions. This represents a significant improvement over conventional systems, which typically fail to serve such users adequately. By extending high-quality recommendations to a broader range of user behaviors, the approach enhances overall recommendation performance and delivers a more satisfying experience across diverse user populations.

## Conclusion

In summary, this disclosure provides a content recommendation method that first recommends content based on average recommendation probability and then collects detailed user feedback—including display and click information such as counts and timing—to determine a sequence of preferred contents for subsequent recommendations. By harnessing this broader spectrum of user feedback, the method achieves effective and reasonable content recommendation even in challenging low-engagement scenarios, thereby improving recommendation performance where traditional click-based methods fall short.

# The Meaning and Use of "Respective"

The word "respective" is one of those small but powerful terms in the English language that helps bring clarity to sentences involving multiple subjects. Understanding how to use it correctly can make writing more precise and professional.

## What Does "Respective" Mean?

The adjective "respective" refers to things that relate individually and separately to two or more people or items that have already been mentioned. It essentially means "belonging or relating separately to each of the people or things previously named."

For example, in the sentence, "The three winners returned to their respective countries," the word "respective" clarifies that each winner went back to their own individual country, not to a shared one.

## Why the Word Matters

The value of "respective" lies in its ability to eliminate confusion. Consider the difference between these two sentences:

- "The students collected their books."
- "The students collected their respective books."

While the first sentence is acceptable, the second makes it absolutely clear that each student picked up their own specific book, rather than a random selection.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid

The most frequent error involves overusing the word when it adds no real value. The phrase "respective" should only appear when there are genuinely multiple parties with separate, corresponding items. Writing "the man returned to his respective home" is incorrect because only one person is involved.

## Conclusion

The word "respective" serves a specific and useful function in communication. When applied thoughtfully, it strengthens clarity and ensures that readers understand exactly how the mentioned people or things connect to their individual counterparts. Mastering such details is part of what separates clear, effective writing from vague and confusing prose.

# Abstract

A content recommendation method and system that leverages user feedback to improve recommendation accuracy is disclosed. The method comprises collecting display information indicating content items presented to a user and click information indicating content items selected by the user during interaction sessions. Based on the collected display and click information, the system computes a feedback signal representing user interest levels for individual content items and content categories. The method further comprises generating a user preference model by analyzing patterns in the display and click information, wherein content items that are displayed but not clicked are assigned negative feedback weights and content items that are clicked are assigned positive feedback weights. The user preference model is dynamically updated as additional feedback is received, enabling the system to adapt to evolving user interests over time. In response to a recommendation request, the system ranks a plurality of candidate content items according to the user preference model and transmits a set of recommended content items to a user device for display. By incorporating both display and click information, the disclosed method reduces recommendation bias, improves click-through rates, and enhances the relevance of recommended content while minimizing the repeated presentation of content items that fail to engage the user.

# Patent Summary: Content Recommendation System

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates to a content recommendation system and method for generating personalized content sequences based on user interaction feedback. More particularly, the invention pertains to a system that collects and processes click feedback and display feedback to construct an ordered sequence of preferred content items for delivery to a user.

### Technical Field

The present disclosure relates generally to information filtering and recommendation systems, and more specifically to systems that dynamically adapt content selection based on implicit and explicit user engagement signals.

### Background

Conventional content recommendation systems often rely on limited feedback signals, resulting in recommendations that fail to accurately reflect evolving user preferences. There exists a need for a system that leverages multiple forms of interaction feedback to more precisely identify and sequence preferred content.

### Overview of the Invention

In one aspect, the invention provides a content recommendation system comprising:

- **A content delivery module** configured to present a plurality of content items to a user through a display interface;

- **A feedback collection module** configured to capture two categories of user interaction data:
  - *Display feedback*, indicating which content items were presented to the user and associated presentation parameters (e.g., duration, position, viewport visibility); and
  - *Click feedback*, indicating which presented content items the user selected or interacted with;

- **A preference analysis module** configured to process the collected display feedback and click feedback to derive engagement metrics for individual content items, wherein a preference indicator is computed based at least in part on a relationship between the number of displays and the number of clicks associated with each content item;

- **A sequence generation module** configured to construct an ordered sequence of preferred content items, wherein the ordering is determined according to the derived preference indicators; and

- **A recommendation output module** configured to deliver the generated sequence to the user through the display interface.

### Method Aspects

In another aspect, the invention provides a method comprising the steps of:

1. Displaying a set of content items to a user;
2. Recording display feedback for each displayed content item;
3. Recording click feedback corresponding to user selections;
4. Computing a preference score for each content item as a function of the recorded display and click feedback;
5. Ranking the content items according to their preference scores; and
6. Assembling and presenting a sequence of preferred content items based on the ranking.

### Advantages

By combining display feedback with click feedback, the disclosed system more accurately distinguishes genuinely preferred content from content that was merely presented, thereby improving the relevance and ordering of recommended content. The resulting sequence of preferred contents may be continuously refined as additional feedback is collected, enabling adaptive, personalized recommendations over time.

# Technical Abstract

## Content Recommendation System Based on Average Recommendation Probability and User Feedback Analysis

The present invention discloses a system and method for recommending content to users based on average recommendation probability derived from aggregated user feedback data. The system addresses limitations in conventional recommendation approaches by dynamically adjusting content selection according to empirically measured user engagement patterns.

The invention operates by collecting feedback data associated with recommended content items, wherein said feedback data comprises display information and interaction information. The display information includes display times (the number of instances a content item is presented to users) and display timing (temporal data indicating when each presentation occurred). The interaction information includes click times (the number of user selections of a content item) and click timing (temporal data indicating when each selection occurred).

Based on the collected feedback data, the system computes an average recommendation probability for each content item, representing the likelihood that a given item will be positively received by users. This probability is calculated as a function of the relationship between click times and display times, optionally weighted by the temporal proximity of display timing and click timing to account for recency and engagement decay.

The system further determines one or more preferred content sequences by ranking and ordering content items according to their respective average recommendation probabilities. These preferred content sequences establish an optimized presentation order that prioritizes content items with higher predicted user engagement.

By continuously incorporating real-time feedback into the average recommendation probability computation, the invention enables adaptive refinement of content recommendations, thereby improving recommendation accuracy, user engagement, and overall system efficiency compared to static recommendation methodologies.

# Summary of the Disclosure

The present disclosure relates to systems and methods for recommending content to users who exhibit few or sparse click behaviors, addressing the technical challenge commonly known as the "cold-start" or "low-activity user" problem in recommendation systems.

In accordance with one aspect of the present disclosure, a computer-implemented method is provided for generating content recommendations for users having limited interaction history. The method comprises identifying a target user associated with a click behavior count below a predetermined threshold, collecting feedback signals associated with the target user, and generating one or more content recommendations based at least in part on the collected feedback signals rather than relying predominantly on historical click data.

In some embodiments, the feedback signals include one or more of explicit feedback and implicit feedback. Explicit feedback may comprise user-provided ratings, likes, dislikes, survey responses, or preference selections. Implicit feedback may comprise dwell time, scroll depth, hover behavior, content skip actions, session duration, or other behavioral indicators that do not require an affirmative click on recommended content.

In another aspect, the method includes constructing a user representation for the target user based on the collected feedback signals, and comparing the user representation against a plurality of content representations to identify candidate content items. In certain embodiments, the user representation is augmented using data derived from a population of users exhibiting similar feedback patterns, thereby enriching an otherwise sparse user profile.

In a further aspect, the disclosure provides a model that is trained to weight feedback signals according to their predictive reliability for low-activity users. The model may be configured to dynamically adjust the relative influence of feedback signals versus click-based signals as a function of the quantity of interaction data available for a given user. As the target user accumulates additional interactions, the system may progressively transition from feedback-driven recommendations toward behavior-driven recommendations.

In yet another aspect, a system is provided comprising one or more processors and a memory storing instructions that, when executed by the one or more processors, cause the system to perform operations including identifying users with few click behaviors, aggregating multi-modal feedback signals, generating candidate recommendations, ranking the candidate recommendations based on predicted user satisfaction, and presenting a ranked set of recommendations to the user through a user interface.

In still another aspect, a non-transitory computer-readable storage medium is provided storing instructions that, when executed by one or more processors, cause the processors to carry out the methods described herein.

Embodiments of the present disclosure provide several technical advantages. By leveraging user feedback signals in place of, or in addition to, sparse click data, the disclosed techniques improve recommendation accuracy and relevance for users who would otherwise be underserved by conventional click-based recommendation systems. The described approaches further enable more efficient utilization of limited user data, reduce the latency associated with building a reliable user profile, and enhance overall user engagement and satisfaction.

The foregoing summary is illustrative only and is not intended to be limiting. Additional aspects, features, and advantages of the disclosed subject matter will become apparent from the following detailed description, the accompanying drawings, and the appended claims.
